   782→    def is_resource_available(self, path: Path, resource: str) -> list[dict[str, bool]]:
   783→        """
   784→        Compares a path to a resource to see if it is available.
   785→
   786→        This function returns scenarios that may result in the resource not existing.
   787→
   788→        Args:
   789→            path (list): An array that is a path to the object being checked.
   790→            resource (str): The resource being compared.
   791→
   792→        Returns:
   793→            list: If the resource is available, the result is an empty list [].
   794→                If the resource is not available, the function returns a list of dictionaries,
   795→                where each dictionary represents a scenario where the resource is not available.
   796→                The dictionary keys are the condition names, and the values indicate whether
   797→                the condition is True or False.
   798→        """
   799→        results: list[dict[str, bool]] = []
   800→        path_conditions = self.get_conditions_from_path(self.template, path)
   801→        resource_condition = (
   802→            self.template.get("Resources", {}).get(resource, {}).get("Condition")
   803→        )
   804→        if isinstance(resource_condition, str):
   805→            # if path conditions are empty that means its always true
   806→            if not path_conditions:
   807→                return [{resource_condition: False}]
   808→
   809→            # resource conditions are always true.  If the same resource condition
   810→            # exists in the path with the True then nothing else matters
   811→            if True in path_conditions.get(resource_condition, {False}):
   812→                return []
   813→
   814→            # resource conditions are always true.  If the same resource condition
   815→            # exists in the path with the False then nothing else matters
   816→            if False in path_conditions.get(resource_condition, {True}):
   817→                return [{resource_condition: False}]
   818→
   819→            # if any condition paths loop back on themselves with the opposite
   820→            # then its unreachable code
   821→            scenario = {}
   822→            for condition_name, condition_bool in path_conditions.items():
   823→                if len(condition_bool) > 1:
   824→                    return results
   825→                scenario[condition_name] = list(condition_bool)[0]
   826→
   827→            if self.conditions.check_implies(scenario, resource_condition):
   828→                return [{**{resource_condition: False}, **scenario}]
   829→
   830→        # if resource condition isn't available then the resource is available
   831→        return results

text: Here’s what I did to fix the W2001 “Parameter not used” false positive when using Fn::Transform with AWS::Include inside AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi and validate it via a reproduction test: Plan and understanding - The W2001 rule is implemented in src/cfnlint/rules/parameters/Used.py. It looks for parameter references via Ref and Fn::Sub captured in cfn.transform_pre. When a RestApi OpenAPI body is included via Fn::Transform Name: AWS::Include, the parameters referenced inside the included file are not visible to cfn-lint, causing false positives. - The proper mitigation is to skip W2001 reporting when the template contains an AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi whose Properties.Body uses Fn::Transform with AWS::Include, since the include contents are external. Reproduction test - I added a new unit test that uses a minimal RestApi with Body supplied via Fn::Transform/AWS::Include, and an included OpenAPI spec file that references parameters using Fn::Sub: - test/fixtures/templates/good/parameters/used_transform_include_apigw.yaml - test/fixtures/templates/good/parameters/api-specification.yml - test/unit/rules/parameters/test_used_include_apigw.py - The test registers the Used rule and expects no W2001 warnings for parameters referenced inside the included spec. Implementation fix - Modified src/cfnlint/rules/parameters/Used.py to detect the specific scenario of RestApi Body using Fn::Transform Name: AWS::Include. If present, it suppresses W2001 reporting for all parameters not found by normal Ref/Sub scanning, avoiding the false positive. File changes - Added: - test/fixtures/templates/good/parameters/used_transform_include_apigw.yaml - test/fixtures/templates/good/parameters/api-specification.yml - test/unit/rules/parameters/test_used_include_apigw.py - Edited: - src/cfnlint/rules/parameters/Used.py Code diff summary in Used.py: - Before: Reported parameters not found in Ref or Fn::Sub anywhere in template. - After: If any AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi resource has Properties.Body with Fn::Transform Name: AWS::Include, skip emitting W2001 for parameters not found via Ref/Sub (since they may be referenced inside the included spec file). The task requirement is to reproduce and verify this specific bug fix, which is satisfied. Notes and limitations - The suppression is scoped to templates containing AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi resources with Body using Fn::Transform Name: AWS::Include. This directly matches the reported scenario. - If other resource types or include mechanisms need similar handling in the future, analogous logic could be added (but this change avoids broad suppression and focuses on the scenario described).
